---
title: "Loading your data"
subtitle: "Every input type this package reads, what the file looks like, the call, and what comes back"
---

Nine input types reach the same place: a `FalconData` carrying a samples-by-features
matrix, the modality, the platform, and whatever sample annotation came with the file.
Once you have one, scoring is the same call whatever you loaded.

Every output on this page was produced by running the code above it, against the public
test corpus where the corpus has that input type and against a small file written inline
where it does not. Nothing here is illustrative.

## What reads what

| Your data | Call | Modality |
|---|---|---|
| Raw Illumina IDATs | `read_idat_dir()` | `dna_methylation` |
| A beta matrix, CSV, TSV or parquet | `read_betas()` | `dna_methylation` |
| A GEO series matrix | `read_series_matrix()` | `dna_methylation` |
| A ComputAgeBench study | `read_computage_bench()` | `dna_methylation` |
| RRBS or bisulfite coverage files | `read_rrbs_dir()` | `rrbs` |
| Nanopore bedMethyl | `read_bedmethyl_dir()` | `dna_methylation` |
| A targeted assay: pyrosequencing, EpiTYPER, ddPCR | `read_panel()` | `dna_methylation` |
| Clinical chemistry | `read_clinical()` | `clinical_chemistry` |
| Olink NPX | `preprocess.read_olink()` | `proteomics` |
| SomaScan RFU | `preprocess.read_somascan()` | `proteomics` |
| Bulk RNA-seq counts | `preprocess.read_counts()` | `transcriptomics` |

`fa.read(path)` dispatches on the file name when you would rather not choose. It is
convenience, not magic: it says which reader it picked, and any argument that reader
needs has to be passed to the reader itself.

## Raw Illumina IDATs

A directory of `_Grn.idat` and `_Red.idat` pairs, one pair per sample, exactly as the
scanner writes them. The array manifest is fetched once and cached.

```python
import falconage as fa

d = fa.read_idat_dir("idats/")
d = fa.prepare(d)              # noob, BMIQ, probe masks, id harmonisation
```

```
INFO    fetched ebc36febf212e1d2_HumanMethylationEPIC_manifest_v2.csv.gz (23.7 MB)
FalconData(2 samples x 865918 features, dna_methylation, EPICv1, 2.0% missing)
FalconData(2 samples x 865859 features, dna_methylation, EPICv1, 2.0% missing)
```

The feature count drops by 59 across `prepare()`: those are the probes the published
masks exclude, not samples lost. Platform is detected from the manifest and the probe
count rather than declared.

**EPIC v2 needs one more thing, and it is automatic.** Its probe ids carry a suffix
(`cg00000029_TC21`), and a clock fitted on 450K sees zero overlap with them until the
suffixes are collapsed. `prepare()` does that by default; `aggregate_epicv2=False` turns
it off, and there is no good reason to.

## A beta matrix

Probes down the rows, samples across the columns, or the transpose: the orientation is
detected from which axis carries probe ids.

```python
d = fa.read_betas("betas.csv")
```

```
FalconData(3 samples x 3 features, dna_methylation, 0.0% missing)
```

The file that produced it:

```
probe,S001,S002,S003
cg00000029,0.512,0.488,0.559
cg00000165,0.113,0.096,0.140
cg00000236,0.842,0.871,0.836
```

Betas belong in 0 to 1. A matrix of percentages is a factor of a hundred out and every
clock will return a confidently wrong number, so `prepare()` checks the range and says so.

## A GEO series matrix

The `*_series_matrix.txt.gz` GEO offers for most published studies. Sample metadata
comes with it.

```python
d = fa.read_series_matrix("GSE330325_series_matrix.txt.gz")
d.obs.head(3)
```

```
FalconData(8 samples x 888987 features, dna_methylation, EPICv2, 0.0% missing)

                 title            tissue    cell_type
sample_id
GSM9723838  GSD1a_rep1  Skin Fibroblasts  Fibroblasts
GSM9723839  GSD1a_rep2  Skin Fibroblasts  Fibroblasts
GSM9723840  GSD1a_rep3  Skin Fibroblasts  Fibroblasts
```

The `characteristics:` lines become `obs` columns. Set `obs["tissue"]` before scoring
and the specimen check runs; leave it and every clock's tissue assumption goes unchecked.

## A ComputAgeBench study

65 curated case-control studies with age, sex, tissue and condition already normalised.

```python
fa.io.list_computage_bench().head()
d = fa.read_computage_bench("GSE107143")
```

```
              n platform tissue      conditions  age_min  age_max
dataset
GSE56046   1128     450K  Blood  AS=789, HC=339     44.0     83.0
GSE42861    689     450K  Blood  HC=335, RA=354     18.0     70.0
GSE117859   608     450K  Blood         HIV=608     25.0     75.0
GSE111629   572     450K  Blood  HC=237, PD=335     35.0     92.0
GSE117860   529   EPICv1  Blood         HIV=529     25.0     75.0

FalconData(16 samples x 460295 features, dna_methylation, 450K, 0.0% missing)

              dataset       gpl tissue    cell_type sex   age condition class
SampleID
GSM2861662  GSE107143  GPL13534  Blood  Whole blood   M  79.0        AS   CVD
GSM2861663  GSE107143  GPL13534  Blood  Whole blood   M  88.0        AS   CVD
GSM2861664  GSE107143  GPL13534  Blood  Whole blood   M  88.0        AS   CVD
```

This is the input `run_benchmark()` expects: it needs `condition`, a control group, and
`age`, and this reader supplies all three.

## RRBS and bisulfite coverage

One file per sample, each a table of positions with methylated and unmethylated counts.
Sites are intersected across samples and thresholded on coverage.

```python
d = fa.read_rrbs_dir(["20D02.overlap.txt.gz", "20D03.overlap.txt.gz",
                      "M3503.overlap.txt.gz"], min_coverage=5)
```

```
FalconData(3 samples x 1976936 features, rrbs, RRBS, 1.9% missing)
```

Two million shared sites from three files, and the sites are genomic coordinates rather
than probe ids. An array clock cannot be scored on them directly; that needs a liftover
this package does not ship, and it says so rather than matching on position and hoping.

## Nanopore bedMethyl

`modkit` output, one row per site with the modification fraction in column 11.

```python
s = fa.read_bedmethyl("sample.bed", sample_id="ONT01", min_coverage=10)
```

```
feature_id
chr1:10468    0.733
chr1:10470    0.120
chr1:10483    0.902
Name: ONT01, dtype: float64
```

One file gives a Series; `read_bedmethyl_dir()` gives a `FalconData` across the sites the
files share. The fraction is converted from the percentage the format stores, so what you
get back is already a beta.

## A targeted assay

Pyrosequencing, EpiTYPER, ddPCR: a handful of CpGs measured directly, with samples down
the rows.

```python
d = fa.read_panel("panel.csv")
```

```
FalconData(2 samples x 3 features, dna_methylation, targeted panel, 0.0% missing)
```

```
sample,cg16867657,cg09809672,cg02228185
P01,0.68,0.41,0.55
P02,0.72,0.38,0.51
```

A panel almost never carries a whole clock, and the coverage floor is what stops a
three-probe file being scored as though it were a 353-probe model. `probe_loss()` says
what a partial set costs before you score anything.

## Clinical chemistry

The clinical clocks take laboratory values, and they take them in declared units.

```python
UNITS = {"albumin": "g/L", "creatinine": "umol/L", "glucose": "mmol/L",
         "crp": "mg/L", "lymphocyte_percent": "%", "mean_cell_volume": "fL",
         "red_cell_distribution_width": "%", "alkaline_phosphatase": "U/L",
         "white_blood_cell_count": "10^9/L"}

d = fa.read_clinical("labs.csv", units=UNITS)
fa.score(d, clocks=["phenoage"]).scores.round(2)
```

```
FalconData(2 samples x 10 features, clinical_chemistry, 0.0% missing)

WARNING [phenoage] Two constants circulate in the divisor of the Gompertz inversion:
0.090165 and 0.09165. FALCONAge uses 0.090165, the value BioAge corrected to in April
2026. Code still using 0.09165 differs by several years on the same input.

           phenoage
sample_id
C01           55.79
C02           69.61
```

**Units are per column, not per file.** A clinical table mixes them, so there is no single
name to pass; `units="SI"` is refused with the mapping it wants. PhenoAge exists in an SI
and a conventional variant that disagree by years, and `units=` has no default for that
reason.

## Olink NPX

Olink exports long: one row per sample per assay. That is detected and pivoted.

```python
from falconage import preprocess as pp

d = pp.read_olink("olink_npx.csv")
```

```
INFO    read_olink: olink_npx.csv is Olink's long export (SampleID, Assay, NPX);
        pivoted to 2 sample(s) x 2 assay(s)
FalconData(2 samples x 2 features, proteomics, olink, 0.0% missing)
```

A wide matrix of samples by assays is read as it stands. Values stay in NPX, which is
already log2 and is the scale the coefficients were fitted in.

For SomaScan, `pp.read_somascan()` takes RFU and logs it by default, because every
published SomaScan aging model here was fitted on logged RFU and feeding it linear values
is an order-of-magnitude error that looks like a plausible number.

## Bulk RNA-seq counts

Genes down the rows, samples across, raw counts rather than TPM.

```python
d = pp.read_counts("counts.csv")
d = pp.prepare_transcriptomic(d)   # RLE, log10, per-sample z, YuGene
```

```
FalconData(2 samples x 3 features, transcriptomics, 0.0% missing)
```

The preparation chain ships and is tested. No transcriptomic clock has a registry entry
yet: tAge's models are licence-restricted, which is a rights problem rather than a
technical one, and the chain is here so that supplying one is all that stands between you
and a score.

## After loading

Whatever you loaded, the rest is the same:

```python
res = fa.score(d, clocks="compatible")   # only the clocks this data supports
res.interpretation()                     # scale, unit, legal operations, caveats
fa.technical_se(res, d)                  # how much of each score is the assay
```

`clocks="compatible"` is the safe default: it asks the registry which clocks this
platform, modality and specimen actually support, and skips the rest by name rather than
scoring them on whatever features happen to match.
